summary: Karnataka Water Watch by Zenith/06 is a satellite-based reservoir monitoring platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 – *Dancing with the SARs*. The project uses NASA-ISRO NISAR Level-2 GCOV Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data to monitor changes in the Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS) reservoir in Karnataka. Unlike optical satellite imagery, SAR can observe the Earth's surface during cloudy monsoon conditions and at any time of day. We process radar backscatter using a fixed −16 dB threshold, apply filtering and spatial masking, and compare water extent across three observations: 23 November 2025, 14 August 2026 and 6 November 2026. Within our approximately 60% reservoir study area, detected water extent decreased from 77.93 km² to 60.62 km²—a reduction of 17.31 km² (22.2%). We developed an interactive web platform featuring date-based water maps, spatial overlap analysis and supporting reservoir-level context. By making satellite-derived water observations accessible and interpretable, Karnataka Water Watch demonstrates how open Earth-observation data can support more informed water-resource monitoring, while clearly communicating the limitations of the analysis.
details:
Karnataka Water Watch: Reservoir Surface Dynamics from Space

NASA International Space Apps Challenge 2026 — "Dancing with the SARs"

Study Focus: Krishnaraja Sagara (KRS) Reservoir, Mandya District, Southern Karnataka, India

Executive Overview

Karnataka Water Watch is an Earth Observation and hydrologic analytics platform engineered to track seasonal surface-water fluctuations, volumetric drawdown, and multi-year drought contraction at the Krishnaraja Sagara (KRS) Reservoir. Built upon NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) L2 Geocoded Backscatter GCOV data, the system bypasses persistent monsoon cloud cover to deliver empirical, all-weather water resource intelligence for one of South India's most critical and contested river basins.

Below are the detailed specifications of the project, addressing its operational mechanics, scientific benefits, intended societal impact, technological stack, creative innovations, and engineering considerations.

1. What Does It Do and How Does It Work?

Operational Mechanics & Physics

Optical Earth observation satellites (e.g., Sentinel-2, Landsat) are frequently blinded by dense tropical monsoon cloud decks at the precise operational windows when reservoirs fill, spill, or experience rapid hydrologic drawdown. Our platform solves this using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR):

- Microwave Penetration: Operates using active L-band microwaves (lambda = 24cm) , which penetrate cloud decks, precipitation, smoke, and nighttime darkness.

- Specular Scattering Mechanism: Calm open water acts as a specular reflector, bouncing incoming radar pulses away from the sensor and yielding low backscatter values -16 dB, In contrast, surrounding rough terrain, rocky outcrops, and agricultural vegetation generate diffuse volume backscatter (substantially brighter pixels, typically 11 dB to 13dB ).

End-to-End Processing Architecture

```

[ NISAR L2 GCOV (Track 12) ]

│

▼

1. Linear-to-dB Power Conversion: γ°_dB = 10 · log10(γ°)

│

▼

2. Calibrated Radiometric Thresholding: Fixed -16.0 dB cutoff on HH co-polarization

│

▼

3. Morphological & Topological Cleanup:

├── 5×5 spatial median filtering (speckle noise reduction)

├── Binary hole closure (< 2,000 px / 0.20 km²)

├── Small-blob false-positive pruning (< 500 px / 0.05 km²)

└── Connected-component analysis (retaining bodies > 5% of primary basin)

│

▼

4. Dam Wall Polyline Geometric Clipping:

└── Vector exclusion along the 2.6 km stone masonry dam crest (pruning downstream canal headworks)

│

▼

5. 7-Class Disjoint Bitmask Classification (Venn partition across 3 epochs)

│

▼

[ Zero-Backend Interactive Dashboard (Leaflet + Chart.js via GitHub Pages) ]

```

1. Data Ingestion: The pipeline ingests NISAR L2 GCOV granules on descending Relative Orbit Track 12 at a calibrated 10.0m times 10.0m spatial pixel spacing.

2. Analysis Epochs: Evaluates three critical operational phases:

- 23 Nov 2025:Post-monsoon baseline near Full Reservoir Level (FRL).

- 14 Aug 2026: Monsoon peak inflow and reservoir refill.

- 06 Nov 2026: Post-monsoon drought contraction.

3. Downstream Canal Elimination: Incorporates an explicit geometric polyline along the 2.6 km stone masonry dam crest. This eliminates 0.95km^2 of false-positive water detections arising from the Visvesvaraya Canal (VC Canal) headworks and downstream post-monsoon irrigated paddy fields.

4. Interactive Disjoint Bitmask Mapping: Outputs the classified surfaces into 7 mutually exclusive, mathematically additive categories (single-date occurrences, pairwise intersections, and a permanent core) rendered as anti-aliased map overlays alongside synchronized telemetry charts.

2. What Benefits Does It Have?

* All-Weather, Cloud-Resilient Monitoring: Eliminates the "monsoon blindness" that cripples optical remote sensing, enabling continuous monitoring during peak rainfall and flooding events.

* Controlled Annual Comparison: By holding orbital geometry constant (Track 12 descending) and comparing identical post-monsoon calendar windows (23 Nov 2025 vs. 06 Nov 2026), the system isolates genuine multi-year environmental drought contraction from seasonal variation.

* High Spatial Resolving Power: At 10m pixel resolution, the model resolves intricate shoreline bathymetry, shallow coves, and river delta channels that coarse-resolution public satellites miss.

* Zero Infrastructure Overhead: All scientific computations are pre-rendered into optimized vector/raster geometries and compact JSON telemetry 10KB. This enables instant load times on edge devices and standard web browsers without requiring cloud servers, database clusters, or paid API keys.

* Exact Mathematical Additivity: Unlike traditional multi-band visualizations that suffer from translucent alpha-blending color bleed, our 7-class disjoint bitmask ensures that the calculated sub-regions sum exactly to the individual epoch totals (pm 0.01km^2).

3. What Is the Intended Impact of the Project?

*Empirical Governance in Contested Water Basins: The Cauvery River basin is historically one of South Asia’s most legally and politically contested water-sharing corridors (between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu). Objective, tamper-proof, radar-derived reservoir area estimates provide unbiased, transparent ground truth for inter-state water regulation, dispute mitigation, and treaty compliance.

*Municipal Drinking Water Security: KRS Reservoir is the primary lifeline supplying drinking water to approximately 14 million residents across Bengaluru and Mysuru. Demonstrating a 17.31km^2 -22.2 net surface water contraction between November 2025 and November 2026 provides municipal water authorities with early-warning indicators of impending supply stress months before peak summer dry seasons.

* Downstream Agrarian Risk Planning: Downstream farmers in the Cauvery Delta rely heavily on predictable irrigation releases. High-resolution surface water monitoring allows agricultural extension bodies to anticipate water rationing and advise farmers on drought-tolerant crop scheduling.

* Operationalizing Flagship Space Missions: Serves as an open-source, scalable operational blueprint for applying upcoming NASA-ISRO NISAR L2 data streams across thousands of ungauged or poorly monitored reservoirs across tropical and subtropical global regions.

4. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software Stack

| Layer | Tools & Technologies | Purpose / Functionality |

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| **Data Sourcing & Archive** | `asf_search` API, NASA Earthdata | Automated querying and bounded spatial subsetting of NISAR L2 GCOV products from the Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF) DAAC. |

| **Core Scientific Pipeline** | **Python 3.10+** | Pipeline scripting, batch data orchestration, and automated statistical validation. |

| **Numeric & Matrix Processing** | **NumPy** | Vectorized linear-to-dB conversion ($\gamma^0_{\text{dB}}$), array slicing, and bitwise binary masking ($2^3 - 1$ classes). |

| **Computer Vision & Filtering** | **SciPy** (`scipy.ndimage`), **OpenCV** | 2D median filtering (despeckling), binary hole filling, connected-component analysis, and 2px anti-aliased shoreline contour tracing. |

| **Geospatial & Projections** | **GDAL / Rasterio**, **PyProj**, **Shapely** | GeoTIFF spatial geocoding, UTM Zone 43N (EPSG:32643) coordinate transforms, bounding box crops, and polyline dam crest intersection. |

| **Cartographic & Frontend** | **HTML5, CSS3, Modern JavaScript (ES6+)** | Responsive user interface, multi-epoch toggle chips, fill vs. outline selectors, and opacity sliders. |

| **Web Mapping & Base Layers** | **Leaflet.js**, **Esri World Imagery** | Keyless, high-resolution interactive satellite basemap integration with sub-pixel georeferenced overlay synchronization. |

| **Data Analytics Visuals** | **Chart.js** | Interactive time-series area charts, gauge correlation metrics, and dynamic legend readouts. |

| **Hosting & Hardware** | Git, **GitHub Pages**, Local Workstation | Entire workflow was executed and verified locally without cloud compute charges; deployed on static, global edge hosting via GitHub Pages. |

---

5. How Is Your Project Creative and Innovative?

1. Multi-Epoch Disjoint Bitmask Classification (Spatial Venn Partition):

Standard change detection commonly relies on simple 2-date difference maps (e.g., green for gain, red for loss). For three or more dates, this typically degenerates into illegible overlapping color transparencies. We developed a 7-class disjoint bitmask partitioning algorithm ($001_2$ through $111_2$) mapped to a carefully selected, color-blind accessible palette (Deep Blue, Golden Orange, Emerald Green, Warm Magenta, Electric Cyan, Vermilion, and Translucent Permanent Core). This provides instant visual differentiation between permanent water, ephemeral monsoon expansion, and multi-year dewatering.

2. Dam Wall Polyline Spatial Audit:

Most automated water segmentation models misclassify downstream canal diversions and flooded agricultural paddies as part of the reservoir surface. We identified that the Visvesvaraya Canal headworks immediately east of the dam crest accounted for 0.95km^2 of false-positive water during November releases. We implemented an automated topological cutoff rule that traces the exact physical masonry dam crest, isolating genuine impoundment storage from downstream conveyance.

3. Physical Wave-Roughening Anomaly Diagnosis:

Rather than silently altering classification thresholds when August 2026 data revealed an unexpected 4.92km^2 missing water patch near the dam wall, the team conducted a detailed backscatter radiometric audit. We discovered that monsoon wind-driven capillary waves elevated surface backscatter by 1.24dB. We documented this scientifically as a physical Bragg-scattering hypothesis rather than smoothing over data anomalies.

4. Hybrid Cartographic Display Modes:

The application enables users to toggle between a filled color-coded disjoint surface and high-contrast 2px anti-aliased shoreline vector contours. The permanent reservoir core is rendered semi-transparently, enabling stakeholders to simultaneously inspect submerged bathymetry and high-resolution optical satellite textures beneath the radar layer.

6. What Factors Did the Team Consider?

* **Polarization Sensitivity (HH vs. HV):

We conducted comparative threshold matrices across co-polarized ($\text{HH}$) and cross-polarized ($\text{HV}$) radar returns. We selected $\text{HH}$ because it exhibits $>8\text{ dB}$ higher land-water backscatter contrast than $\text{HV}$. Cross-pol ($\text{HV}$) was rejected for water delineation because volume scattering from surrounding dry scrubland and crops caused severe boundary bleeding ($>180\text{ km}^2$ false water detected at standard thresholds).

* **Threshold Stability & Strict Monotonicity:**

We verified our fixed $-16.0\text{ dB}$ threshold against a sensitivity matrix ranging from $-14.0\text{ dB}$ to $-24.0\text{ dB}$. Across all tested thresholds, the relative surface ordering ($\text{Nov 2025} > \text{Aug 2026} > \text{Nov 2026}$) remained strictly monotonic, validating that observed surface contractions reflect true environmental dynamics rather than thresholding artifacts.

* **Frame Boundary Truncation vs. Published Spread:**

KRS Reservoir has a published Full Reservoir Level spread of $129.5\text{ km}^2$. However, the NISAR Track 12 granule boundary terminates at $76.450^\circ\text{E}$, observing a maximum of $77.93\text{ km}^2$ within our study box ($60.2\%$ of published FRL area; approximately $40\%$ truncated along the western Hemavathi/Cauvery arms). We explicitly labeled all metrics across the code, charts, and user interface as *"within study box"* to maintain complete scientific integrity.

* **Ground Truth & Capacity Metrics:**

Satellite observations were cross-referenced against historical gauge records from the Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre (KSNDMC) and Central Water Commission (CWC). We carefully reconciled reported media percentages by differentiating between **Gross Storage Capacity (49.452 TMC)** and **Live/Effective Storage Capacity (45.070 TMC)**, confirming that our detected surface areas directionally matched reported storage drawdowns (~124 ft near FRL in Nov 2025 vs. ~98–99 ft during drought in Nov 2026).

* **Bandwidth & Compute Constraints:**

Because full NISAR HDF5 granules average ~6.7 GB each, attempting to stream or process raw data client-side would fail on constrained network connections. We designed the pipeline to perform bounded spatial subsetting upfront, decoupling data-heavy scientific raster transformations from client-side visual exploration.

Key Scientific Findings Summary

| Acquisition Date | NISAR Detected Area *(Within Study Box)* | Storage & Reservoir State | Measured Hydrologic Change |

| :--- | :---: | :--- | :---: |

| **23 Nov 2025** | **77.93 km²** | Near Full Reservoir Level (FRL ~124 ft) | *Baseline Epoch* |

| **14 Aug 2026** | **62.72 km²** | Monsoon refill / wind-roughened surface | $-15.21\text{ km}^2$ ($-19.5\%$) |

| **06 Nov 2026** | **60.62 km²** | Post-monsoon regional drought contraction | **$-17.31\text{ km}^2$ ($-22.2\%$)** |

* **Shoreline Dewatering:** Comparing identical post-monsoon dates (Nov 2025 to Nov 2026) under identical viewing angles isolates 18.03km^2 of exposed shoreline mudflats and dried inlets** over a **$54.98\text{ km}^2$ stable core reservoir basin**.
